en: Homage to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta!
Then the glorious Vajradhara, the supreme tamer of the difficult to tame,
the hero who conquers the three worlds, the king of secrets, and the lord of the vajra— || 1 ||
With eyes like fully blossomed white lotuses and a face like a wide-open lotus, he repeatedly brandished his excellent vajra with his hand. || 2 ||
Accompanied by infinite Vajrapāṇis led by Bhṛkuṭītaraṅga, who are heroes capable of subduing the unsubdued, possessing heroic and loathsome forms. || 3 ||
With their own hands brandishing the tips of flashing vajras, they are supreme, performing the welfare of the world through wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion. (4)

Together with the Protectors who possess bodies bent in prostration, who act for the sake of the Buddha’s work, and who—though appearing in forms of wrathful conflict—are joyful, satisfied in their intentions, and gladdened. (5)
Having prostrated before the Lord, the Fully Awakened One, the Blessed Tathāgata,
he stood before him with palms joined in reverence and spoke these words.
For my benefit, for my sake, and out of compassion for me, O Lord, [teach] so that I may become one who has attained the perfect awakening to the net of illusion. (7)
For the benefit of all sentient beings who are submerged in the mire of ignorance and whose minds are agitated by the afflictions, and for the attainment of the unsurpassed fruit. (8)

May the Perfectly Awakened One, the Blessed One, the Teacher, the Guru of the World—supreme knower of the reality of the great commitments and master of the dispositions of the faculties—reveal it. (6)
Of the Wisdom-Body of the Blessed One, the Great Uṣṇīṣa, the Lord of Speech, Mañjuśrī the Knowledge-Being, the embodiment of wisdom, the Self-Existent One. || 10 ||
The supreme *Nāmasaṅgīti*, which possesses profound meaning, exalted meaning, and great meaning; which is peerless and auspicious;
and which is virtuous in the beginning, middle, and end—was spoken by the Buddhas of the past, and indeed will be spoken by those of the future.
And those who are currently enraged speak it again and again. || 12 ||
That which is fully proclaimed in this *Māyājāla-mahātantra* by the immeasurable, joyful holders of mantras who are great Vajradharas. (13)
And I, firm in my resolve, shall maintain this vow until its final fulfillment, so that I may become, O Lord, a holder of the secrets of all the perfectly awakened ones. (14)
I shall reveal [this] for the sake of sentient beings, according to the particularity of their inclinations, for the destruction of all afflictions and for the abandonment of all ignorance. 15.

Having thus entreated the Tathāgata, Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, with palms joined in reverence, stood before him with his body bowed low. The *Paramārthanāmasaṃgīti* of Mañjuśrījñānasattva is finished. 16.
The sixteen verses of entreaty.
Then the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, the perfectly awakened one, the supreme among bipeds—

Mahā-maha-mahā-ma, Mahā-maha-mahā-tra, Mahā-maha-mahā-la, the one of great form, the one of great name, the Great One, the wielder of the weapon of great wisdom, the one of great fame— extended from his own auspicious mouth his long, broad, and beautiful tongue. 17.
The Great Desire, displaying a great smile that purifies the three lower realms for all worlds, illuminates the threefold world and subdues the enemy of the four Māras. (18)
With a sweet voice that filled the three worlds,
Brahmā addressed the lord of the Guhyakas, the mighty Vajrapāṇi.
Excellent, O glorious Vajradhara! Excellent to you, O Vajrapāṇi, you who, endowed with great compassion, act for the sake of the welfare of the world. (20)
You are now prepared to hear from me the *Saṅgīti* named *Mahārtha*, which is purifying and destroys all evil, belonging to Mañjuśrī, the Wisdom Body. (21)
"Therefore, O Lord of Guhyakas, I shall teach this well to you;
listen with a one-pointed mind. "Very well, Blessed One," [he replied]. (22)
Six verses of response.
Then the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, having surveyed the entire great family of mantras, the family of mantra-holders and vidyādharas, and the three families, [spoke]. (23)
The family of the mundane and supramundane, the great family of the light of the world;
the supreme family of Mahāmudrā, and the great family of Mahoṣṇīṣa. || 24 ||

The Lord of the ten stages, purified by the ten knowledges, possessing ten aspects, accomplishing the welfare of the entire world in its tenfold entirety, beginningless, the speaker of reality as it is—homage to him!
raḥ | The Lord || 1 ||
Repeatedly. || 2 ||
With the [suffixes] ṇi and bhiḥ. || 3 ||
By means of the *noti*s; by means of the *pi*s; [the *ḥ*]. || 5 ||
[It is] manifest. || 6 ||
That [is] a heavy syllable preceded by a short vowel.
Of the Lord.
Of the world. || 10 ||
—Śivā.
|| This is the *Mañjuśrījñānasattvasya-paramārthanāmasaṃgīti*. Having joined his palms in reverence, he stood before him with his body prostrated. (16)
The sixteen verses of entreaty.
Then the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, the perfectly enlightened one, the supreme among bipeds;
the great festival, the great delusion, the destroyer of the delusion of those with deluded minds;
the great festival, the great wrath, the great enemy of wrath—[he is] the Great One. (31)
The Great Sacrifice, the great greed that destroys all greed,
having extended his beautiful, long, and broad tongue from his auspicious mouth— 17.
Great desire, great bliss, great joy, and great delight. || 32 ||
Displaying a smile that purifies the three lower realms for all beings, which illuminates the three worlds and subdues the four Māras, [he spoke]. (18)
With a sweet, divine voice that filled the three worlds,
he addressed the Lord of Secrets, the mighty Vajrapāṇi.
Excellent, O glorious Vajradhara! Excellent to you, O Vajrapāṇi, you who, endowed with great compassion, act for the benefit of the world. (20)
You are prepared to hear from me the *Saṅgīti* named *Mahārthā*, which is purifying and destroys all evil, belonging to the wisdom-body of Mañjuśrī. (21)
"Therefore, O Lord of Guhyakas, I shall teach this to you;
listen with a one-pointed mind. "Very well, Blessed One," [he replied]. || 22 ||
Six verses of response.
Then the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, having surveyed the entire great family of mantras, the family of mantra-holders and vidyādharas, and the three families.
The family of the mundane and supramundane, the great family of the light of the world and beyond, the supreme family of Mahāmudrā, and the great family of Mahoṣṇīṣa. || 24 ||
Two verses on the contemplation of the six families.
He spoke this verse of the Lord of Speech, which is joined with these six mantra-kings, which arises as non-duality, and whose nature is non-arising. (25)
A, Ā, I, Ī, U, Ū, E, AI, O, AU, AṂ, AḤ—these are situated in the heart as the supreme [vowels]. || 11 ||
I am the embodiment of wisdom, the Buddha of all Buddhas residing in the three times. || 26 ||
Oṃ, homage to you, the embodiment of the wisdom-knowledge that cuts through suffering with a vajra-sharpness, the Lord of Speech of the Knowledge-Body (Jñānakāya), Arapacana! || 27 ||
But they have not yet arrived. || 12 ||
It is sung by the Ṛṣis. || 13 ||
The third section is concluded: the three verses on the sequence of awakening through the net of illusion.
That is to say: the Blessed One, the Buddha, the Perfectly Awakened One, is born from the syllable *A*;
the syllable *A* is the foremost of all letters, of great significance, and the supreme syllable. (28)
For the Great Breath is indeed non-arising, devoid of vocal utterance; it is the fire that consumes all causes of expression, and it is the supreme luminosity of all speech. || 26 ||
The great festival of great passion, who brings delight to all sentient beings;
the great delusion of great hatred, the great enemy of all afflictions. || 30 ||
Of great form, of great body, of great color, of great stature, of great name, most noble, and possessing a vast and expansive mandala. || 33 ||
He who wields the great weapon of wisdom, the supreme goad for the great afflictions, of great renown, of great fame, of great light, and of great splendor. || 34 ||

The wise one who possesses great illusion, the accomplisher of the purpose of great illusion, he who delights in the pleasure of great illusion, and the master of the great illusion of Indra’s net. || 35 ||
The supreme lord of great generosity, the foremost upholder of great ethical discipline, the steadfast bearer of great patience, and one whose prowess is great vigor. || 36 ||

Abiding in the samādhi of great meditation, possessing the body of great wisdom, he is of great power, possesses great skillful means, is the embodiment of aspiration, and is an ocean of knowledge. || 37 ||
He consists of great loving-kindness, he is the object of measure, the greatly compassionate one of supreme intellect;
he possesses great wisdom, great intelligence, great skillful means, and is a great achiever. || 38 ||
Endowed with the power of great supernatural faculties, possessing great speed and great velocity, he is of great prosperity, of great renown, and of great strength and prowess. || 39 ||
The shatterer of the great mountain of existence, the dense holder of the great vajra, the greatly fierce, the greatly terrible, the inspirer of fear in those who cause great fear. || 40 ||
The Lord is the supreme among great vidyās, the Guru is the supreme among great mantras;
he has ascended the path of the Mahāyāna and is the highest of the Mahāyāna systems. || 41 ||
The Fourteen Verses on the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.

Buddha Mahāvairocana, the great sage, the great silent one; he who has attained the ten perfections, who is the locus of the ten perfections, who is the purity of the ten perfections, and who is the method of the ten perfections. || 43 ||
The Lord is the master of the ten stages, established upon the ten stages;
his self is purified by the ten knowledges, and he upholds the purity of the ten knowledges. || 44 ||

The Lord of Munis has ten aspects, is the goal of the ten goals, possesses the ten powers, and is all-pervading; he accomplishes the welfare of the entire universe, masters the ten aspects, and is great. (45)
He is beginningless, of a nature free from conceptual proliferation, of a pure nature, and of the nature of suchness;
he is a speaker of reality, one who speaks as he acts, and whose word is never otherwise.
Non-dual and a proponent of non-duality, he is established in the limit of reality; with the lion’s roar of selflessness, he terrifies the deer-like followers of false paths. (47)
All-pervading, with unfailing movement, possessing the speed of the mind of a Tathāgata, the Victor who has conquered the enemy, the triumphant universal monarch of great power. || 48 ||

The leader of the hosts, the teacher of the hosts, the lord of the hosts, the master of the hosts, self-controlled, of great majesty, the foremost, not to be led by others, and the one of the great path. || 46 ||
Lord of Speech, Master of Speech, Eloquent One, Lord of Words, of infinite voice, truthful in speech, speaker of truth, and teacher of the Four Truths. || 50 ||
For he is one who does not fall back, a non-returner, a rhinoceros-like solitary leader;
having emerged through various means of deliverance, he is the single cause of the great elements, the Great Element itself. 51.
The Arhat, the monk whose outflows are exhausted, free from passion and with senses conquered, is the supreme bearer of the Three Jewels and the teacher of the highest of the three vehicles. || 65 ||

Amoghapāśa, the Victorious One, Vajrapāśa, the Great Seizer, Vajrāṅkuśa, the Great Noose; these are twenty-five verses minus one-quarter, concerning the Gāthās on the Wisdom of the Perfectly Pure Dharmadhātu; [he who is] Vajrabhairava, the Terrifier. 66.
The King of Wrath, six-faced, terrifying, six-eyed, six-armed, and powerful; his skeleton formidable with fangs, and possessing a hundred faces like the Halāhala poison. || 67 ||
Yamāntaka, King of Obstacles, Vajravega, the Terrifying One, Vighuṣṭavajra, Hṛdvajra, Māyāvajra, and Mahodara. || 68 ||
The Lord of the Thunderbolt, the source of the Vajra, the essence of the Vajra, like unto the sky;
possessing the majesty of a single immovable matted lock, he wears a fresh elephant hide as a garment. || 66 ||
He has attained security, attained fearlessness, become cooled, and is indeed undisturbed;
there is the most terrible cry of "Hāhā," the terrifying sound of "Hīhī," the loud laughter of "Aṭṭa," the great laughter, the diamond-like laugh, and the great roar. || 70 ||
Vajrasattva, the Great Being; Vajrarāja, the Great Bliss;
Vajracaṇḍa, the Great Joy; Vajra Hūṃkāra, the Performer of Hūṃ. || 71 ||

He who wields the vajra and the arrow-weapon, the vajra-sword that cuts through all, the bearer of the universal vajra, the wielder of the vajra, the sole vajra-holder, the vanquisher in battle. || 72 ||
He whose eyes are formidable with vajra-flames, whose hair is vajra-flames, who possesses the vajra-penetration and the great penetration, who has a hundred eyes and vajra-eyes. || 73 ||
His body is marked with hair like a vajra; his form consists of a single vajra-hair;
he has the onset of vajra-pointed nails; and his skin is as solid as the essence of a vajra. || 74 ||
The glorious one who wears a garland of vajras, adorned with vajra ornaments, whose roar is the loud laughter of "hā hā," the resonance of the vajra, the six-syllabled one. || 75 ||
He of the gentle voice, the great roar, the single great sound of the three worlds; his voice extends to the limits of the realm of space, he who is the best among those possessed of voice. || 76 ||
Endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, the supreme knower of the world, is free from possessiveness and free from egoism, established in the method of the two truths. || 53 ||

He stands at the far shore of saṃsāra; he has accomplished all that was to be done; he stands on firm ground; he is steeped in the knowledge of absolute liberation (kaivalya); and he rends asunder with the weapon of wisdom. || 54 ||

The True Dharma is the King of Dharma, radiant, the supreme illuminator of the world and beyond; it is the Lord of Dharma, the King of Dharma, and the instructor of the path to the highest good. || 55 ||
Siddhārtha, whose resolve is accomplished, who is free from all conceptual constructs, the non-conceptual, inexhaustible element—the supreme, imperishable realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu). || 56 ||

Possessing merit, he is one who has accumulated the equipment of merit; possessing great knowledge, he is a mine of wisdom; possessing knowledge, he is a knower of the real and the unreal—one who has fully gathered the two accumulations. || 57 ||

He is eternal, the sovereign of the universe, the yogi, meditation itself, the object of meditation, and the lord of the intellects; he is to be realized within one's own self, immovable, the supreme primordial one, and the bearer of the three bodies.
[Blank]
The Buddha consists of the five bodies; the all-pervading Lord consists of the five gnoses;
he has the five Buddhas as his crown and the five eyes of unimpeded vision.
The progenitor of all Buddhas, the supreme and most excellent son of the Buddha, born from the source of wisdom, unborn, the source of Dharma, he who brings an end to existence. || 60 ||
The bull among proponents of emptiness, whose roar is profound and sublime. || 77 ||
[The text provided consists solely of two vertical bars (||), which in this context function as a punctuation mark indicating the end of a section or verse. [End of Section]
The verses on mirror-like wisdom number ten and a quarter minus one quarter.

Suchness, the reality of selflessness, the limit of reality, the ineffable; the conch of Dharma with its great sound, the gong of Dharma with its great resonance; the non-abiding nirvāṇa, the drum of Dharma in the ten directions. || 78 ||
Formless yet possessing form, the foremost, manifold in form, mind-made, the glory that illuminates all forms, he who bears the reflection of everything without exception. || 76 ||
Invincible, of great majesty, the Great Lord of the three realms, established on the exalted Noble Path, the banner of Dharma, the source of great prosperity. || 80 ||
The body of the sole youth of the three worlds, the ancient, the aged, the Lord of Creatures;
the body of the sole youth of the three worlds, the essence of the cloud, the diamond-natured, the Lord of the World born instantly;
self-arisen from the sky, the great fire of wisdom and primordial gnosis.
Vairocana is of great brilliance; he is the radiance of the light of gnosis.
He is the lamp of the world, the torch of gnosis, possessed of great splendor, and luminous. || 62 ||
The King of Knowledge, the foremost Lord of Mantras, the King of Mantras who accomplishes the great purpose; the Great Uṣṇīṣa, the Wondrous Uṣṇīṣa, the All-Seeing, the Lord of Space. || 63 ||
The fire of the essential nature of all Buddhas, whose eyes are the joy of the world, who possesses the universal form, the creator, the one worthy of worship and honor—the great Ṛṣi. || 64 ||
Bearing the thirty-two marks, he is lovely, the most beautiful in the three worlds. || 81 ||
The mantra-practitioner who upholds the three lineages, who maintains the great samaya-mantras,
is a teacher of worldly knowledge and qualities, a teacher of the world, and one who is confident and fearless.

The Lord is the protector; he is the expanse of the sky; he has shattered the shell of the egg of ignorance; he is the consecration of all-encompassing knowledge; he is the cessation of the suffering of the three types of suffering; he is the removal of all obscurations; he is the destroyer of all afflictions; he is the mother of all sentient beings; he is free from all limiting adjuncts; he is the Great Thought; he is the Great Eon; he knows the welfare of all sentient beings; he knows the auspicious and the inauspicious; he knows the faculties of sentient beings; he is the possessor of qualities; he knows all qualities; he is the source of all auspiciousness; he is the great festival; he is the worthy recipient of honor; he is the most excellent; he is the giver of boons; he is the enemy of the great terrors; he is the crest; he is the flame; he is the five-faced one.

He is the upholder of the great vows, the one of great austerity, the knower of Brahman; he is liberation, release, and extinction; he is the conqueror of pleasure and pain, the partless, the stainless hero, the perfectly awakened one whose nature is pure knowledge, free from conceptual construction, without beginning or end, whose sole eye is wisdom. 65.
And twenty-five;
The syllable *ra* following *bhuja* and *balī* is a *ra-gaṇa*. || 68 ||
To you.
Ruhah || 73 ||
traḥ || 74 ||
Abandonment.
— ten.
He who:
The husband is the one who protects from fear. || 81 ||
The ultimate *Nāmasaṃgīti* of Mañjuśrījñānasattva: the Lord, the Protector, attained by the three worlds, the refuge, the Savior, the unsurpassed. 82.
He whose enjoyment is the expanse of the sky, an ocean of omniscient wisdom, the breaker of the shell of the egg of ignorance, and the shatterer of the cage of existence. || 83 ||

He who has pacified all afflictions, who has reached the further shore of the ocean of saṃsāra, whose crown is the consecration of primordial wisdom, and who is adorned by perfect enlightenment. || 84 ||

He is the pacifier of the suffering of the three types of suffering, the triple end, the infinite, the one who has attained the three liberations, who is free from all obscurations, and has reached equality with space. || 85 ||

He has transcended the flow of the impurities of all afflictions and the course of the three times and the pathless; he is the great elephant among all beings, the crest-jewel upon the crest of the assembly. || 86 ||
Completely liberated from all limiting adjuncts, well-established on the path of space, the omnipresent Lord is the bearer of the great wish-fulfilling gem, the most excellent of all jewels. || 87 ||

He is the flourishing great kalpa-tree, the supreme and most auspicious jar, the creator who accomplishes the welfare of all sentient beings, the seeker of their benefit, and the one who is affectionate toward all beings. || 88 ||

He knows the auspicious and the inauspicious; he knows the time, he knows the occasion, and he is the master who observes the commitments; he knows the faculties of sentient beings, he knows the proper moment, and he is skilled in the three types of liberation. || 86 ||

He is possessed of virtues, a knower of virtues, a knower of Dharma, praised, the source of auspiciousness, the most auspicious of all auspicious things, fame, fortune, glory, and the auspicious one. 60.
He is the great festival, the great relief, the great bliss, the great delight; he is honor, hospitality, prosperity, joy, glory, and the Lord of Fame. || 61 ||

He is the one to be chosen, the giver of boons, the most excellent, the worthy refuge, the supreme protector, the foremost enemy of great fear, and the destroyer of all fears without exception. || 82 ||
He has a crest, he wears a topknot, he has matted locks, he is shaggy-haired, he is shaven-headed, and he wears a diadem;
he is five-faced, he has five tufts of hair, and he has five locks of matted hair as his crown.

Observing the great vows, wearing the girdle of muñja grass, a celibate student of the highest vows, a performer of great austerities, devoted to penance, a graduate (snātaka), Gautama was the foremost leader. || 64 ||
The knower of Brahman is a Brāhmaṇa; he is Brahmā, having attained the nirvāṇa of Brahman. He is liberation, release, the limb of liberation, emancipation, tranquility, and the auspicious. || 65 ||

It is cessation, liberation, peace, the highest good, the final departure, the end-maker, the bringer of an end to pleasure and pain, the ultimate goal, dispassion, and the exhaustion of the substrates of existence. || 66 ||
[Blank]
Unconquerable, incomparable, unmanifest, without appearance, stainless, partless, all-pervasive, subtle, the seed, and free from outflows. || 67 ||
Free from passion, stainless, immaculate, with faults cast out, free from disease, perfectly awakened, one whose self is enlightened, omniscient, all-knowing, and supreme. || 68 ||

Transcending the nature of consciousness, wisdom maintains a non-dual form; it is free from conceptual construction, effortless, and performs the activities of the perfectly awakened ones throughout the three times. || 66 ||
The Buddha is without beginning or end, the primordial Buddha, devoid of causal succession;
he is the stainless eye of sole gnosis, the embodiment of gnosis, the Tathāgata. || 100 ||
Lord of speech, great debater, king of debaters, bull among debaters, the best of those who speak, most excellent, lion of debaters, unconquered. || 101 ||
Samantadarśin, Pramodita, Tejomālin, Sudarśana, Śrīvatsa, Suprabha, Dīpti, Bhā, and Bhāsvarakaradyuti. || 102 ||
The supreme and most excellent great physician, the peerless remover of the arrow [of suffering], the tree of all medicinal herbs, and the great enemy of the disease of the afflictions. || 103 ||
The beloved ornament of the three worlds, glorious, a circle of stars, reaching to the ends of the ten directions and the sky, he is the lofty, great banner of the Dharma. (104)
Vast as the parasol over the world, a mandala of loving-kindness and compassion, the glorious Padmanarteśvara, the great sovereign with a jewel parasol. || 105 ||
The great king of all Buddhas, who maintains the essential nature of all Buddhas;
the great yoga of all Buddhas, the sole teaching of all Buddhas. || 106 ||
The glory of the vajra-jewel consecration, the sovereign lord of all jewels, the lord of the lords of all worlds, the supreme master of all vajra-holders. || 107 ||
The great mind of all Buddhas, the mental range of all Buddhas, the great body of all Buddhas, and the eloquence of all Buddhas. || 108 ||
The Vajra-Sun, the great illuminator, possessing the stainless radiance of the Vajra-Moon;
he is the Great Passion beginning with dispassion, blazing with light of every color. || 106 ||

The perfectly awakened one in the vajra posture, upholder of the Dharma through the Buddha’s assembly, born from the lotus of the Buddhas, the glorious one who holds the treasury of omniscient wisdom. || 110 ||
The King who possesses all illusions, the great holder of the Buddha's wisdom, the sharp vajra, the great sword, the pure, the supreme syllable. || 111 ||
The one who cuts through suffering, the Great Vehicle, the Vajra-Dharma, and the great weapon;
the Victor over the Māras, profound as a vajra, possessing vajra-like intelligence, and knowing things as they truly are. || 112 ||

He who has fulfilled all the perfections, who is adorned with all the stages, whose nature is the purity of the selflessness of phenomena, and whose heart radiates the light of the moon of perfect gnosis. || 113 ||
The great exertion of the net of illusion, the supreme lord of all tantras, seated upon the vajra-throne of the entirety, who maintains the body of inexhaustible gnosis. || 114 ||
Samantabhadra, the one of excellent intellect, Kṣitigarbha, the sustainer of the world, the great womb of all Buddhas, and the bearer of the wheel of universal emanations. || 115 ||
The supreme essence of the nature of all things, the upholder of the nature of all things;
he whose nature is non-arising, who exists for the sake of the universe, and who upholds the nature of all phenomena. 116.

Possessing great wisdom in a single moment, upholding the realization of all phenomena, the sage who has reached the limit of reality is the supreme intellect, the full comprehension of all phenomena. (117)
Stable, with a perfectly serene self, he upholds the awakening of the perfectly enlightened ones;
he is directly perceived by all Buddhas, a flame of wisdom, brilliantly radiant. || 118 ||
[The text provided consists of two vertical bars (||), which in classical Indian scripts typically mark the end of a section or verse. [End of Section]
The forty-two verses on the wisdom of discernment.
The bull among men bowed down. || 101 ||
Rśanaḥ—splendor. || 102 ||
He overcomes physical injury.
The circle is the most excellent. || 104 ||
The All-pervading Lord. || 105 ||
Nabhaḥ-prabha (the one with the luster of the sky). || 106 ||
The supreme achiever of desired goals, the purifier of all misfortunes, the Lord who is the highest among all beings, the liberator of all sentient beings. || 116 ||

The sole hero in the battle against the afflictions, the destroyer of the pride of the enemy of ignorance—this is the *Nāmasaṃgīti* of Mañjuśrī, the Knowledge Being, which accomplishes the welfare of the world through the flood of wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion. (137)

He whose purpose is the abandonment of all conceptualizations, whose purpose is consciousness, who maintains cessation, who is the object of the minds of all sentient beings, and who moves within the minds of all sentient beings. || 138 ||
The intellect (dhīḥ) is the glorious one who assumes the erotic sentiment (śṛṅgāra), and takes on the forms of the heroic (vīra) and the loathsome (bībhatsa). || 120 ||
Abiding within the minds of all sentient beings, having entered into the state of equality with their thoughts,
he casts out hundreds of long arms and dances with every step; possessing the expansive majesty of a hundred glorious arms, he dances across the vast expanse of the sky.
He stands with the surface of the entire earth's circle covered by the sole of one foot, while his big toe-nail rests upon the summit of the cosmic egg. || 122 ||

The single meaning is the non-dual meaning of the Dharma, the ultimate reality that is indestructible; yet the continuity of mind and consciousness appears as the objects of various representations and forms. || 123 ||

He finds delight in the meaning of all phenomena without exception, delights in emptiness, possesses supreme intelligence, has transcended the passion for existence and so forth, and takes great delight in the three realms of existence. || 124 ||
Possessing the brilliant luster of the rays of the autumnal moon, pure and white as a clear cloud,
he has the splendor of the orb of the rising sun and the radiance of great passion in his nails.
With hair as dark as the crest of a sapphire and locks like great sapphires, he possesses the splendor of the rays of a great jewel; adorned with the emanations of the Buddha.

He causes hundreds of world-systems to tremble; his great stride is the basis of miraculous power; he gladdens the minds of all sentient beings and brings delight to the minds of all sentient beings. || 136 ||

The established conclusion is free from delusion, devoid of all error, characterized by a mind beyond doubt, possessing three objects, being the object of all things, and consisting of the three qualities. || 140 ||
The meaning of the five aggregates is the three times; he who manifests all moments, is perfectly awakened in a single moment, and maintains the intrinsic nature of all Buddhas. || 141 ||
Bodyless yet the foremost of bodies, the manifester of millions of bodies;
he who displays all forms, the great jewel-bannered one, the great gem.
The twenty-four verses on the wisdom of equality.

He is that which all the perfectly awakened ones must realize; he is the unsurpassed awakening of the Buddhas, the syllable-less source of mantras, and the three families of the great mantras. || 143 ||
The progenitor of the meaning of all mantras is the great bindu, which is without syllables;
it is the five-syllabled great void, the bindu-void, and the six-syllabled. || 144 ||
He possesses all forms yet is formless; he bears the sixteen, the half, and the quarter-bindu;
he is the bearer of great mindfulness, the reality, and the sovereign of the fourfold mindfulness and samādhi.
He is timeless, beyond all calculation, and the upholder of the pinnacle of the fourth dhyāna.
He is the fragrance of the flowers of the factors of enlightenment, an ocean of the qualities of the Tathāgatas, and the possessor of the six [perfections]. || 110 ||
He who knows the method of the eightfold path, he who knows the path of the perfectly awakened one.
Kṣīraḥ || 111 ||
He has great attachment for all sentient beings, yet he is free from attachment like space;
he is born from the minds of all sentient beings and possesses the speed of the minds of all sentient beings.

He who knows the faculties and objects of all sentient beings; he who captivates the minds of all sentient beings; he who is proficient in the arts of all meditations; he who knows the lineages and families of samādhis;
he whose body is the supreme body of samādhi; the sovereign of all saṃbhogakāyas.

The Nirmāṇakāya is the foremost body, the upholder of the lineage of the Buddha’s emanations; manifesting throughout the universe in the ten directions, he acts for the benefit of the world according to its needs.
The god beyond gods, the lord of gods, the sovereign of the Suras, the ruler of the Dānavas, and the knower of the ultimate goal. 112.
He who knows the reality of the meaning of the five aggregates, he who maintains the purity of the five aggregates. || 130 ||
The lord of the immortals, the preceptor of the gods, the destroyer, and the sovereign of the destroyers.
He whose radiance is like that of the letter *t*. || 113 ||
The one who upholds the supreme. || 114 ||
du-dhṛtiḥ -dhṛk || 115 ||
Free from attachment, he stands at the limit of all deliverance; he is skilled in all deliverance,
established on the path of all deliverance, and the teacher of all deliverance.

He has uprooted existence with its twelve links, maintains the purity of the twelve aspects, possesses the form of the method of the four truths, and maintains the realization of the eight knowledges. || 132 ||
He who knows the meaning of the truths in twelve aspects and understands reality in sixteen aspects;
he who has crossed the wilderness of existence, the unique Teacher, the Guru of the World,
renowned throughout the ten directions, the great Lord of the Gift of Dharma.
Girt with the armor of loving-kindness, clad in the mail of compassion,
and wielding the sword, bow, and arrows of wisdom, he vanquishes the battle of afflictions and ignorance.
The enemy of Māra, the conqueror of Māra, the hero who brings an end to the fear of the four Māras,
the one awakened through the twenty modes of enlightenment, the fully enlightened one, the all-knowing, the supreme. || 133 ||
The Fully Awakened One, the leader of the world, is the conqueror of all the armies of Māra. || 151 ||
He is the one who manifests millions of immeasurable Buddha-nirmāṇakāyas and holds a boat. 116.
He is the realization of all moments [of existence], the knower of the meaning of every moment of mind.
The intellect [is] ...-k. || 117 ||
Holding the awakening of the Vajra,
he manifests the welfare of the world through the various methods and means of the diverse vehicles; having emerged from the three vehicles, he abides in the fruit of the single vehicle.
The self whose nature is purified of the realm of afflictions, who brings about the exhaustion of the realm of karma, is radiant. || 118 ||
He has completely crossed over the ocean of the floods and emerged from the wilderness of yoga.
Forty.
Having completely abandoned the afflictions, the secondary afflictions, and all defilements along with their latent tendencies,
he is to be saluted, worshipped, and greeted; he is to be honored at all times, most worthy of veneration, respected, and prostrated to— the supreme teacher.

He whose stride traverses the three worlds alone, whose prowess extends to the limits of space, who possesses the three types of knowledge, who is learned in the Vedas, who is pure, who possesses the six supernormal powers, and who possesses the six recollections. || 153 ||
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has transcended the world, possesses great supernatural power,
is established in the perfection of wisdom, and has attained the true nature of wisdom.

The knower of self, the knower of others, all-encompassing, more pervasive than all, indeed the foremost of persons, transcending all comparison, the supreme lord of knowledge— such is he to be known. || 155 ||
The Lord of the gift of Dharma is supreme, the teacher of the meaning of the four seals, the most worthy of veneration by the worlds of those who follow the three vehicles of departure. (156)

Mañjuśrī, the supreme among the illustrious, is the great glory purified in the ultimate sense; he is the fortunate one of the three worlds, the bestower of all prosperity, and the possessor of splendor. || 157 ||
The fifteen verses on the knowledge of the performance of duties.
Homage to you, the granter of boons, the diamond-like essence; homage be to you, O limit of reality!
Homage to you, whose womb is emptiness; homage be to you, the awakening of the Buddhas. || 158 ||
O Buddha-passion, homage be to you; O Buddha-desire, salutations again and again. O Buddha-joy, homage be to you; O Buddha-delight, salutations again and again.
O Buddha’s smile, homage to you; O Buddha’s laugh, homage again and again. O Buddha’s speech, may there be homage to you; O Buddha’s being, homage again and again.
Homage be to you, O source of non-existence; homage to you, O source of awakening;
homage to you, O source from space; homage to you, O source of primordial wisdom.
Homage to you, the net of illusion; homage to you, the Buddha’s drama; homage to you, O All, to all; homage be to you, the body of gnosis. || 162 ||
Thus are the five verses on the wisdom of the five Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, vajra of the purity of the intrinsic nature of the non-existence of all phenomena; a ā aṃ aḥ—all phenomena are primordially pure;
Mañjuśrī, the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas, the purity of wisdom—take that, aṃ aḥ! Take the heart of all Tathāgatas, hara hara!

Oṃ hūṃ hrīḥ! O Blessed One, embodiment of primordial wisdom, Lord of Speech, Great Utterance, you who are as stainless as the sky regarding all phenomena, the essence of the gnosis of the utterly pure realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu)! Āḥ! This is the arrangement of the mantra.

Then the glorious Vajradhara, joyful and satisfied, with palms joined in reverence, paid homage to the Lord, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Mañjuśrījñānasattva, [and recited] the *Nāmasaṃgīti*, the ultimate reality. (163)
Together with many other lords, such as Guhyendra and Vajrapāṇi,
along with the retinues of the wrathful kings, he spoke these words aloud:
We rejoice, O Lord; well said, well said! A great benefit has been conferred upon us, which leads to the attainment of perfect enlightenment.
And for this world which is without a protector and yearns for the fruit of liberation, this pure path to the highest good has been proclaimed through the method of the Net of Illusion. (166)
Profound, sublime, and vast, of great significance and accomplishing the welfare of the world— this is indeed the domain of the Buddhas, taught by the Perfectly Enlightened One. || 167 ||
Thus end the five summary verses.

The *Nāmasaṃgīti*, the ultimate reality of the Blessed One Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, from the chapter on the Net of Samādhis contained within the sixteen-thousand-verse *Ārya-māyājāla* Mahāyoga Tantra, spoken by the Blessed Tathāgata Śākyamuni, is hereby completed.
